Resolves #20124

`ScrollManager#onContainerScroll` (vertical and horizontal branches) and `ScrollManager#onScrollEnd` now update `isScrolling` across `bodyStart`, `bodyEnd`, and `body` via `#setBodyScrolling` (`setSilent({isScrolling})`), and `View#syncBodies` updates `scrollLeft`/`scrollTop` via `_body.setSilent({scrollLeft, scrollTop})`. This keeps `Body#afterSetIsScrolling` updating `vdom.cls` and firing `isScrollingChange` synchronously without launching a colliding depth-1 child VDOM flight ahead of `View#syncBodies`, so `_body.createViewData(true, force)` runs synchronously and the `neo-is-scrolling` class delta ships inside the single `View` VDOM batch.

Evidence: L2 (verified via Playwright unit suite in `ScrollFlightMerge.spec.mjs`, `ScrollManagerHoverSyncRouting.spec.mjs`, and `AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs`) → L2 required (all close-target ACs are unit-covered in CI).

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `src/grid/ScrollManager.mjs` (`#setBodyScrolling` called in `onContainerScroll` vertical/horizontal branches and `onScrollEnd`) and `src/grid/View.mjs` (`_body.setSilent({scrollLeft, scrollTop})` in `syncBodies`) |
| AC-2 | `test/playwright/unit/grid/ScrollFlightMerge.spec.mjs` › *ScrollManager onContainerScroll from rest and onScrollEnd ship neo-is-scrolling inside the single View flight without child-update collision* (`body.isVdomUpdating === false`, `VDomUpdate.preUpdateMap.has(body.id) === false`, `VDomUpdate.postUpdateQueueMap.get(body.id) === null`, `batches === [[view.id]]`) |
| AC-3 | `test/playwright/unit/grid/ScrollFlightMerge.spec.mjs` › *ScrollManager onContainerScroll from rest and onScrollEnd ship neo-is-scrolling inside the single View flight without child-update collision* (`batches === [[view.id], [view.id]]`, `body.vnode.className` removes `neo-is-scrolling`) |
| AC-4 | `test/playwright/unit/grid/ScrollFlightMerge.spec.mjs` and `test/playwright/unit/grid/AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs` (11/11 pass; 339/339 `unit/grid/` pass) |

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Request Changes
- **Rationale**: The fix is right and well proven: a silent `isScrolling` plus a silent `syncBodies` write lets the `View`'s single dense flight carry the class and the rows, and the new spec catches the regression red-first. Two small shape items keep it from merging as is. Production code branches for a plain-object test double, which the core-idiom audit makes a Required Action. And the ticket's ledger promises an inline comment in `syncBodies` that the diff does not add. Both are in-place edits worth fixing before merge, so this is neither a follow-up nor an approval with nits.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Thanks, Julia. This is a clean diagnosis: the six-step collision walk in #20124 matched the source line for line, and the spec measures the actual batches rather than a flag. Two small shape items below.

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #20124 with its Contract Ledger and Avoided Traps; `dev` `ScrollManager#onContainerScroll` / `#onScrollEnd` / `#syncGridBody`; `View#syncBodies` and its depth comment; `Body#afterSetIsScrolling`; the existing `ScrollFlightMerge.spec.mjs` (#18439 / #18719); `ScrollManagerHoverSyncRouting.spec.mjs`; the core-idiom audit. Memory Core sweep: no prior decision making the toggle deliberately non-silent.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Keep `View#syncBodies` the single transaction owner. The scroll-time `isScrolling` toggles and the body coordinate writes record `needsVdomUpdate` silently instead of launching their own flights, so one `View` update at `ROW_DISTANCE + maxCellDepth` ships the class and the rows. Silence must not leak to direct `body.isScrolling` writers (AnimateRows), and every silent mark needs a guaranteed following `View` update, or `neo-is-scrolling` can get stuck. Tests should count real batches and the vnode class, not internal flags.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **Matches**, with two shape deviations. `syncBodies` has no early return and always ends in `me.update()` (`View.mjs:1296`), so every silent mark is flushed, including on scroll end. The spec asserts `[[view.id]]` for the first frame and `[[view.id],[view.id]]` after `onScrollEnd`, with the class arriving in and then leaving `body.vnode.className`. The deviations are the `setSilent ? … : …` branch in `#setBodyScrolling` and the missing `syncBodies` comment (RA-1, RA-2).
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The premise is measured as batches, and red-first is shown below. It also keeps one owner per transaction, which is the engine's own stated design (`View.mjs:1278`).

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: the `View.mjs` edit applies to every `syncBodies` caller, not only the scroll path. I checked that it is safe: `setSilent` still runs `afterSetScrollLeft`/`afterSetScrollTop`, and the trailing `me.update()` covers the bodies at full row depth. But a `syncBodies` caller that had relied on `_body.set` to flush an unrelated pending body update ahead of the `View` now ships it inside the `View` flight.
